Thanks again for the demo earlier — the latency numbers looked promising and the team is excited to try a short evaluation. We discussed building a MAP that ties milestone acceptance to a ramped commit (monthly TPM). To get internal buy-in on our side I need a concrete proposal showing:

- Evaluation window (length + success criteria)
- Proposed monthly TPM targets during evaluation and for the subsequent ramp (6 months)
- Pricing tiers and discount triggers tied to cumulative commits/milestones
- Any initial ramp credits or safety valve for quality/regression that we can call out in the MAP

Hi Sofia — thanks for the clear brief and the attachment. Appreciate the traffic shape reference; that helps a lot.

I've sketched a MAP that links evaluation sign-offs to a staged commercial commitment. Key points below (formal MAP + spreadsheet attached):

- Evaluation: 8-week PoC (weeks 1–8) with success criteria: 95th percentile latency < 400ms on your p95 request mix and quality pass rate >= 92% on the provided prompt set.
- Trial capacity: Up to 500k TPM burst available during PoC; sustained evaluation target = 300k TPM/month.
- Ramp (months 1–6 post-eval): target monthly TPMs = [Month1: 750k, Month2: 1.25M, Month3: 2.0M, Month4: 2.75M, Month5: 3.5M, Month6: 4.0M].
- Pricing & discount triggers (applied to per-token price):
  * Base list price = $0.00022 / token (hosted API)
  * 5% commit discount once cumulative monthly average >= 1M TPM for two consecutive months
  * 10% commit discount at sustained >= 3M TPM average over a rolling 3-month window
  * Ramp credit: one-time $15k usage credit applied if Greenline reaches Month3 target within 90 days of go-live (designed as an adoption incentive).
- SLA & fallbacks: we propose an initial 99.5% availability SLO for dedicated routing; automatic fallback to compatible model variants if capacity constrained (full details in MAP).

Open items for procurement/finance: final approval on the one-time credit (finance OK?), and whether Greenline requires any longer pricing guarantees beyond 12 months. Marcus/Monica/Rishi — can you confirm cost-of-service margin at these tiered discounts and whether the $15k credit is approvable?

I attached a TPM trajectory sheet (TPM_trajectory.xlsx) and the MAP PDF with milestones and acceptance criteria. If that looks good to you, I'll prepare a DocuSign SOW that encodes the MAP milestones and the discount trigger language.

Next steps: Sofia — can we lock a 30-minute review with Procurement early next week (Mon/Tue)?

Thanks,
Olga
Olga Petrov
Sr. Account Exec, Redwood Inference
